finding.title: A chat comment ending in the retry request is misread as a retry and forced to JSON
finding.body: The `endsWith` check can't tell the host's own retry prompt from a user comment: a chat prompt built from a comment ending in the RESUBMIT_REQUEST sentence ends the same way, so the chat answer is coerced into a ReviewSubmission JSON object and posted verbatim as the bot's reply on the PR. Distinguish the retry prompt from a user comment, e.g. by matching the full prompt shape or tagging the message.
finding.basis: isResubmitPrompt (src/review/prompt.ts:51-53) tests only `text.endsWith(RESUBMIT_REQUEST)`. Failure scenario: a commenter posts a comment whose text ends with "Call submit_review now with the review, and don't write it out as a message."; the chat branch (src/pull-request.ts:568-582) prompts with answerPrompt(author, text, skill), whose trailing text is exactly that sentence, so awaitsResubmission (src/models.ts:33-36) matches, the model's answer is forced to a ReviewSubmission JSON object, and the raw JSON is posted to the PR as the bot's reply. The check needs to distinguish the host's own retry prompt from a user comment, e.g. by matching the full prompt shape or tagging the message.

finding.title: Retry detection matches any user text ending in the resubmit sentence
finding.body: isResubmitPrompt identifies the retry prompt by its trailing sentence alone, so any user-authored text that happens to end with that sentence is treated as a resubmission request. A cheaper discriminator: the real retry prompt always starts with one of the two outcome lines in resubmitPrompt, so requiring that prefix (or the full prompt text) removes the collision. In practice this forces a JSON answer to a chat comment, which the commenter sees as an unreadable JSON blob.
finding.basis: Scenario: a commenter ends their comment with the sentence "Call submit_review now with the review, and don't write it out as a message." finding.title: Spreading undefined options can throw at runtime
finding.body: When `streamSimple` is called without an `options` argument (common in the codebase), `options` is `undefined`. Replace the spread with a safe default, e.g. `{ ...(options ?? {}), samplingParams: { ...(options?.samplingParams ?? {}), response_format: REVIEW_AS_JSON } }`.

finding.body: Keep the `await` so the posted marker is durable before `pending` is deleted and before the post-prompt check at line 228 reads it; nothing here depends on saving one await.
finding.basis: Failure scenario: `review()` (R228) checks `storage.get(`posted:${pr.head.sha}`)` after the prompt to decide between logging "posted" and calling `reportUnpostedReview`. Because the put is not awaited, the read at R228 can race the write and see the key absent even though the review was created, logging a false "review.failed"/no_submission outcome. finding.title: Retry JSON with rejected findings is dropped without the rejections pass
finding.body: If the retry's JSON contains findings that fail `validateFindings` (a bad quote, a wrong path, more than 25 findings), `postReview` returns `rejectionsText`, marks `rejectionsReturned` on the pending review, and `postedRetryText` merely logs `review.retry_text_refused` and returns false, after which `askAgain` goes straight to `reportUnpostedReview`. The whole review is then dropped even though most findings may be fine, and the one-time rejections pass is consumed without the model ever seeing it — the first-run text path (finishReview → askAgain) does re-ask in this situation. Consider re-prompting once with the rejection text here, or not setting `rejectionsReturned` when the caller is the retry-text path.
finding.basis: postReview returns rejectionsText after setting rejectionsReturned=true (src/pull-request.ts:222-225), and the caller here only logs and gives up; the model is never shown the rejection text (it arrived on a text path, not as a tool result).

finding.quote: it("lifts a request for changes whatever the model's verdict", () => {
finding.title: decideApproval is never tested with a commented record that carried an approve verdict
finding.body: The linked issue asks that "unit tests cover each branch of the decision". The path through `recordWait` where a `COMMENT` record with `verdict: "approve"` passes on to the live checks is only covered indirectly via the `awaitsApproval` tests; no `decideApproval` test drives that branch. Add one case, e.g. `expect(outcome({ ...ready, lastReview: { ...requested, event: "COMMENT", verdict: "approve" } })).toEqual({ kind: "approve" })`, so the lifted-comment path through the full decision fails loudly if `recordWait` regresses.
finding.basis: Issue #25 states: "Unit tests cover each branch of the decision." In recordWait, the branch where a COMMENT record with verdict "approve" passes (so the decision continues to the live checks and can approve) is only exercised indirectly through awaitsApproval; every decideApproval test either starts from the REQUEST_CHANGES ready state or tests review_stands with verdict "comment".

findings.evidence: #25 asks for a decision test through a commented approve record
findings.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,235 @@
+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest"
+import type { CheckRunSummary } from "../src/github/client.ts"
+import {
+  awaitsApproval,
+  checksState,
+  decideApproval,
+  evaluatesAfterReview,
+  lastReviewOf,
+  openBlockingIn,
+  verdictAfterChecks,
+  type ApprovalState,
+  type LastReview,
+} from "../src/review/approval.ts"
+import type { FindingInput } from "../src/review/findings.ts"
+import type { OpenThread } from "../src/review/incremental.ts"
+
+const requested: LastReview = {
+  reviewId: 1,
+  event: "REQUEST_CHANGES",
+  headSha: "bbb",
+  verdict: "request_changes",
+  heldBack: 0,
+  at: 1,
+}
+
+const ready: ApprovalState = {
+  workflow: true,
+  paused: false,
+  open: true,
+  reviewInFlight: false,
+  headSha: "bbb",
+  reviewedHead: "bbb",
+  lastReview: requested,
+  openBlocking: 0,
+  checks: "passing",
+}
+
+function outcome(state: ApprovalState): string {
+  const decision = decideApproval(state)
+  return decision.kind === "wait" ? decision.reason : decision.kind
+}
+
+describe("decideApproval", () => {
+  it("approves a reviewed head whose request for changes has nothing left behind it", () => {
+    expect(decideApproval(ready)).toEqual({ kind: "approve" })
+  })
+
+  it("never approves when the request-changes workflow is off", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, workflow: false })).toBe("workflow_off")
+  })
+
+  it("does nothing while paused", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, paused: true })).toBe("paused")
+  })
+
+  it("never approves a pull request that is closed, merged or a draft", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, open: false })).toBe("not_open")
+  })
+
+  it("waits for a review in flight, which evaluates when it ends", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, reviewInFlight: true })).toBe("review_in_flight")
+  })
+
+  it("waits for the review of the current head when the head isn't the reviewed one", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, reviewedHead: "aaa" })).toBe("not_reviewed")
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, reviewedHead: undefined })).toBe("not_reviewed")
+  })
+
+  it("waits for a review that records itself, as on a pull request last reviewed before this shipped", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, lastReview: undefined })).toBe("no_record")
+  })
+
+  it("never approves twice, whether the last approval is of this head or an earlier one", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, lastReview: { ...requested, event: "APPROVE" } })).toBe("approved")
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, lastReview: { ...requested, event: "APPROVE", headSha: "aaa" } })).toBe("approved")
+  })
+
+  it("lets a review that only commented stand until the next review", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, lastReview: { ...requested, event: "COMMENT", verdict: "comment" } })).toBe(
+      "review_stands",
+    )
+  })
+
+  it("never approves when the threads couldn't be read", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, openBlocking: "unknown" })).toBe("threads_unknown")
+  })
+
+  it("waits while one of andabot's blocking threads is open", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, openBlocking: 1 })).toBe("blocking_threads")
+  })
+
+  it("never approves when the check runs couldn't be read", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, checks: "unknown" })).toBe("checks_unknown")
+  })
+
+  it("waits on a failing check", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, checks: "failing" })).toBe("checks_failing")
+  })
+
+  it("waits for checks still running", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, checks: "pending" })).toBe("checks_pending")
+  })
+
+  it("reports the first reason that holds", () => {
+    expect(outcome({ ...ready, paused: true, openBlocking: 1, checks: "failing" })).toBe("paused")
+  })
+})
+
+describe("awaitsApproval", () => {
+  it("lifts a request for changes whatever the model's verdict", () => {
+    for (const verdict of ["approve", "request_changes", "comment"] as const) {
+      expect(awaitsApproval({ ...requested, verdict })).toBe(true)
+    }
+  })
+
+  it("lifts a comment only when the model meant to approve", () => {
+    const commented: LastReview = { reviewId: 1, event: "COMMENT", headSha: "bbb", heldBack: 0, at: 1 }
+    expect(awaitsApproval({ ...commented, verdict: "approve" })).toBe(true)
+    expect(awaitsApproval({ ...commented, verdict: "comment" })).toBe(false)
+    expect(awaitsApproval({ ...commented, verdict: "request_changes" })).toBe(false)
+    expect(awaitsApproval(commented)).toBe(false)
+  })
+
+  it("never lifts a review that held a finding back", () => {
+    expect(awaitsApproval({ ...requested, heldBack: 1 })).toBe(false)
+  })
+
+  it("never lifts an approval", () => {
+    expect(awaitsApproval({ ...requested, event: "APPROVE" })).toBe(false)
+  })
+})
+
+function checkRun(overrides: Partial<CheckRunSummary> = {}): CheckRunSummary {
+  return { name: "check", status: "completed", conclusion: "success", app: "github-actions", ...overrides }
+}
+
+describe("checksState", () => {
+  it("passes with no runs, or with only andabot's own still running", () => {
+    expect(checksState([], "andabot")).toBe("passing")
+    expect(checksState([checkRun({ app: "andabot", status: "in_progress", conclusion: null })], "andabot")).toBe(
+      "passing",
+    )
+  })
+
+  it("passes when every other run completed as success, neutral or skipped", () => {
+    const runs = ["success", "neutral", "skipped"].map((conclusion) => checkRun({ conclusion }))
+    expect(checksState(runs, "andabot")).toBe("passing")
+  })
+
+  it("fails on a completed run with any other conclusion, stale included", () => {
+    expect(checksState([checkRun({ conclusion: "failure" })], "andabot")).toBe("failing")
+    expect(checksState([checkRun({ conclusion: "stale" })], "andabot")).toBe("failing")
+  })
+
+  it("counts a run with no app as another app's", () => {
+    expect(checksState([checkRun({ app: null, conclusion: "failure" })], "andabot")).toBe("failing")
+  })
+
+  it("waits for a run that hasn't completed", () => {
+    expect(checksState([checkRun({ status: "queued", conclusion: null })], "andabot")).toBe("pending")
+  })
+
+  it("reports failing over pending", () => {
+    const runs = [checkRun({ status: "queued", conclusion: null }), checkRun({ conclusion: "failure" })]
+    expect(checksState(runs, "andabot")).toBe("failing")
+  })
+})
+
+function thread(handle: string, blocking: boolean): OpenThread {
+  return {
+    handle,
+    threadId: `id-${handle}`,
+    firstCommentId: 1,
+    path: "a.ts",
+    line: 1,
+    side: "RIGHT",
+    outdated: false,
+    title: "t",
+    blocking,
+  }
+}
+
+describe("openBlockingIn", () => {
+  it("counts the open blocking threads, or unknown when they couldn't be read", () => {
+    expect(openBlockingIn(undefined)).toBe("unknown")
+    expect(openBlockingIn({ open: [thread("T1", true), thread("T2", false)], recheck: [] })).toBe(1)
+  })
+})
+
+function finding(severity: FindingInput["severity"]): FindingInput {
+  return { path: "a.ts", line: 1, quote: "q", basis_kind: "defect", basis: "b", severity, title: "t", body: "b" }
+}
+
+describe("lastReviewOf", () => {
+  it("counts only the rejections that hold approval back", () => {
+    const rejected = [
+      { finding: finding("blocking"), reason: "r", unfounded: false },
+      { finding: finding("blocking"), reason: "r", unfounded: true },
+      { finding: finding("suggestion"), reason: "r", unfounded: false },
+    ]
+    expect(
+      lastReviewOf({
+        reviewId: 9,
+        event: "REQUEST_CHANGES",
+        headSha: "bbb",
+        verdict: "request_changes",
+        rejected,
+        at: 5,
+      }),
+    ).toEqual({ reviewId: 9, event: "REQUEST_CHANGES", headSha: "bbb", verdict: "request_changes", heldBack: 1, at: 5 })
+  })
+})
+
+describe("verdictAfterChecks", () => {
+  it("holds a clean review's approval until the checks pass", () => {
+    expect(verdictAfterChecks("APPROVE", "passing")).toBe("APPROVE")
+    for (const checks of ["pending", "failing", "unknown"] as const) {
+      expect(verdictAfterChecks("APPROVE", checks)).toBe("AWAITING_CHECKS")
+    }
+  })
+
+  it("leaves a request for changes and a comment as they are", () => {
+    expect(verdictAfterChecks("REQUEST_CHANGES", undefined)).toBe("REQUEST_CHANGES")
+    expect(verdictAfterChecks("COMMENT", "failing")).toBe("COMMENT")
+  })
+})
+
+describe("evaluatesAfterReview", () => {
+  it("evaluates after a review that didn't approve, unless it just posted a blocking finding", () => {
+    expect(evaluatesAfterReview("APPROVE", [])).toBe(false)
+    expect(evaluatesAfterReview("REQUEST_CHANGES", [finding("blocking")])).toBe(false)
+    expect(evaluatesAfterReview("REQUEST_CHANGES", [finding("suggestion")])).toBe(true)
+    expect(evaluatesAfterReview("COMMENT", [])).toBe(true)
+  })
+})

finding.quote: ? `on \`${thread.path}\`, on a line the latest push no longer shows`
finding.title: File-level comments are answered with a wrong "line no longer shows" claim
finding.body: `line === null` is used to mean both "the thread is outdated" and "the comment has no line at all". For an outdated thread the wording is right; for a file-level review comment (GitHub omits `line`) it tells the model something false about the thread. The PR description flags this as deferred and unverified, but it is easy to handle now: distinguish `line: null` set by the router from an explicitly absent line, or word the branch neutrally ("on `path`, not attached to a line of the current diff").
finding.basis: A review comment with no `line` (a file-level comment) passes `threadContextOf` with `line: null` and is answered from a prompt that states the latest push no longer shows the line — a false statement the model may repeat. Expected: the prompt describes a file-level comment as file-level.

findings.evidence: #63 code reports a false outdated-thread state for file comments

finding.title: Rounding clamp can mislabel a priced model as unpriced
finding.body: `isUnpriced` treats `usd === 0` as "no price", but `modelSpend` clamps the ledger's dollar delta to 0 whenever `after.usd` is fractionally below `before.usd` — exactly the float-rounding case the round-clamp test builds (`0.1 + 0.2` vs `0.3`). With tokens grown and the clamped delta at 0, a priced model is labelled unpriced. Distinguish "the ledger reports no cost" from "the price is unknown": treat a tiny nonzero delta as priced (e.g. `spend.usd > 0 || spend.usd < 0`), or carry the raw (unclamped) delta and let the display handle the sign.
finding.basis: spendSince({}, { glm: { input: 100, output: 10, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, usd: 0.1 + 0.2 } }, new Map([["glm", 1]])) followed by after { input: 100, output: 20, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, usd: 0.3 }: modelSpend clamps usd to max(0, 0.3 - 0.30000000000000004) = 0 while outputTokens is 10, so isUnpriced returns true and the footer says "cost unknown" for a priced model. Expected "≈ 0 neurons" or similar, not an unpriced claim.

@@ -0,0 +1,174 @@
+import type { AssistantMessage } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai"
+import type { EntryRecord, UsageState } from "@earendil-works/pi-durable"
+import { Type, type Static } from "typebox"
+import type { LogFields } from "../log.ts"
+
+const USD_PER_THOUSAND_NEURONS = 0.011
+
+const UsageTally = Type.Object({
+  input: Type.Integer(),
+  output: Type.Integer(),
+  cacheRead: Type.Integer(),
+  cacheWrite: Type.Integer(),
+  usd: Type.Number(),
+})
+
+type UsageTally = Static<typeof UsageTally>
+
+export const UsageTotals = Type.Record(Type.String(), UsageTally)
+
+export type UsageTotals = Static<typeof UsageTotals>
+
+const ModelSpend = Type.Object({
+  model: Type.String(),
+  calls: Type.Integer(),
+  inputTokens: Type.Integer(),
+  cachedTokens: Type.Integer(),
+  outputTokens: Type.Integer(),
+  usd: Type.Number(),
+})
+
+export type ModelSpend = Static<typeof ModelSpend>
+
+export const ReviewSpend = Type.Array(ModelSpend)
+
+export type ReviewSpend = Static<typeof ReviewSpend>
+
+const NO_USAGE: UsageTally = { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, usd: 0 }
+
+export function usageTotals(state: Pick<UsageState, "models">): UsageTotals {
+  return Object.fromEntries(
+    Object.entries(state.models).map(([model, usage]) => [
+      model,
+      {
+        input: usage.input,
+        output: usage.output,
+        cacheRead: usage.cacheRead,
+        cacheWrite: usage.cacheWrite,
+        usd: usage.cost.total,
+      },
+    ]),
+  )
+}
+
+export function callsByModel(entries: readonly Pick<EntryRecord, "model">[]): Map<string, number> {
+  const calls = new Map<string, number>()
+  for (const message of entries.flatMap((entry) => entry.model ?? []).filter(isAssistant)) {
+    const model = `${message.provider}/${message.model}`
+    calls.set(model, (calls.get(model) ?? 0) + 1)
+  }
+  return calls
+}
+
+export function spendSince(before: UsageTotals, after: UsageTotals, calls: ReadonlyMap<string, number>): ReviewSpend {
+  const models = [...new Set([...Object.keys(after), ...calls.keys()])]
+  return models
+    .map((model) => modelSpend(model, before[model] ?? NO_USAGE, after[model] ?? NO_USAGE, calls.get(model) ?? 0))
+    .filter((spend) => spend.calls > 0 || tokensOf(spend) > 0)
+}
+
+function modelSpend(model: string, before: UsageTally, after: UsageTally, calls: number): ModelSpend {
+  const grown = (key: keyof UsageTally) => Math.max(0, after[key] - before[key])
+  return {
+    model,
+    calls,
+    inputTokens: grown("input") + grown("cacheRead") + grown("cacheWrite"),
+    cachedTokens: grown("cacheRead"),
+    outputTokens: grown("output"),
+    usd: grown("usd"),
+  }
+}
+
+interface SpendTotals {
+  calls: number
+  inputTokens: number
+  cachedTokens: number
+  outputTokens: number
+  usd: number
+  unpriced: string[]
+}
+
+function totalsOf(spend: ReviewSpend): SpendTotals {
+  return {
+    calls: sum(spend, (model) => model.calls),
+    inputTokens: sum(spend, (model) => model.inputTokens),
+    cachedTokens: sum(spend, (model) => model.cachedTokens),
+    outputTokens: sum(spend, (model) => model.outputTokens),
+    usd: sum(spend, (model) => model.usd),
+    unpriced: spend.filter(isUnpriced).map((model) => model.model),
+  }
+}
+
+export function spendLine(spend: ReviewSpend): string | undefined {
+  if (spend.length === 0) return undefined
+  const totals = totalsOf(spend)
+  const calls = `${totals.calls} model call${totals.calls === 1 ? "" : "s"}`
+  if (tokensOf(totals) === 0) return `${calls} · usage not reported`
+  const tokens = `${tokenCount(totals.inputTokens)} in / ${tokenCount(totals.outputTokens)} out tokens`
+  return [calls, tokens, priceText(totals, spend.length)].join(" · ")
+}
+
+function priceText(totals: SpendTotals, models: number): string {
+  if (totals.unpriced.length === models) return "cost unknown"
+  const price = `${neuronText(neuronsOf(totals.usd))} (${dollarText(totals.usd)})`
+  if (totals.unpriced.length === 0) return price
+  return `${price} + unpriced ${totals.unpriced.map(modelName).join(", ")}`
+}
+
+export function spendFields(spend: ReviewSpend | undefined): LogFields {
+  if (spend === undefined || spend.length === 0) return {}
+  const totals = totalsOf(spend)
+  const fields: LogFields = {
+    calls: totals.calls,
+    inputTokens: totals.inputTokens,
+    cachedTokens: totals.cachedTokens,
+    outputTokens: totals.outputTokens,
+    models: spend.map((model) => `${model.model}:${model.calls}`).join(" "),
+  }
+  if (totals.unpriced.length > 0 || tokensOf(totals) === 0) return fields
+  return { ...fields, neurons: Math.round(neuronsOf(totals.usd) * 10) / 10, usd: totals.usd }
+}
+
+function isUnpriced(spend: ModelSpend): boolean {
+  return tokensOf(spend) > 0 && spend.usd === 0
+}
+
+function tokensOf(spend: Pick<ModelSpend, "inputTokens" | "outputTokens">): number {
+  return spend.inputTokens + spend.outputTokens
+}
+
+function neuronsOf(usd: number): number {
+  return (usd / USD_PER_THOUSAND_NEURONS) * 1000
+}
+
+function neuronText(neurons: number): string {
+  const rounded = Math.round(neurons)
+  return rounded === 0 ? "< 1 neuron" : `≈ ${rounded.toLocaleString("en-US")} neurons`
+}
+
+function dollarText(usd: number): string {
+  return usd < 0.0005 ? "<$0.001" : `$${usd.toFixed(3)}`
+}
+
+function tokenCount(tokens: number): string {
+  if (tokens < 1_000) return String(tokens)
+  if (tokens < 9_950) return `${tenths(tokens / 1_000)}k`
+  if (tokens < 999_500) return `${Math.round(tokens / 1_000)}k`
+  return `${tenths(tokens / 1_000_000)}M`
+}
+
+function tenths(value: number): string {
+  return value.toFixed(1).replace(/\.0$/, "")
+}
+
+function modelName(model: string): string {
+  return model.slice(model.indexOf("/") + 1)
+}
+
+function sum(spend: ReviewSpend, count: (model: ModelSpend) => number): number {
+  return spend.reduce((total, model) => total + count(model), 0)
+}
+
+function isAssistant(message: NonNullable<EntryRecord["model"]>[number]): message is AssistantMessage {
+  return message.role === "assistant"
+}

findings.issue:
#32: Show what each review cost in the summary comment
Nothing says what a review cost. The runs recorded on #2 list "Neurons: see the Workers AI dashboard (Andrew)", and the dashboard can't tie spend to one review. `docs/design.md`: "Costs are tracked per conversation in Pi's `pi.usage` document, so the summary comment can print what the review cost." Comparing models in #2 needs this, since Kimi K2.7 Code reviews take far longer than gpt-oss-120b's.

## What to do

1. **Read usage.** Read `pi.usage` for the review's operations, including the retry: model calls, and input and output tokens per model.
2. **Price it.** Convert tokens to neurons and dollars from a per-model price table in code, with the Workers AI pricing page as its source. Show "unknown" for a model that isn't in the table.
3. **Show it.** Put a line in the summary footer, for example "3 model calls · 31k in / 4k out tokens · ≈ 1,200 neurons". Log the same in `review.done`.

## Done when

- Unit tests cover the calculation and the footer line, including a model with no price.
- A posted review's footer shows its calls and tokens, and #2's next run records cost from it.

finding.title: Unreadable-ledger behaviour ships without a test
finding.body: The description promises "If the ledger can't be read, the review still posts, without the cost line" and "a review with no `usageBefore` posts without the line", but nothing exercises those paths — the `usage_unreadable` log, the `{}` return, or the `spendOf` short-circuit on a pending record with no baseline. These live on `PullRequest`, so if the existing harness has a way to stub `pi()`/`session()` failures, add a test for each branch; at minimum note that these paths ship untested.

No test fails if the try/catch branches regress.

finding.quote: if (!(await this.isRootConversation(conversationId))) return { text: NOT_IN_FLIGHT_REFUSAL, done: false }
finding.title: New root-conversation guard on submit_review has no test
finding.body: This guard is the defence in depth the design relies on so a summary session can never post a review: it is what keeps a `submit_review` call from the summary session (or any other conversation) out of the review path. Nothing fails if someone drops it or inverts the comparison. The repository tests the object's pure decisions heavily but has no object tests, so at minimum a test at the seam this PR already creates would help — e.g. by driving `submitReview` (or the tool's execute) with a non-root conversation id and expecting the refusal text and `done: false`.
finding.basis: New behaviour without a test: no test exercises a submit_review call whose conversationId is not the root conversation's, so the summary-session and root-conversation guards (with callerIsReviewInFlight) can regress without a failing test. The design's test list (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-commands-design.md) names "submit_review refusing a call from outside the root conversation, if that's the guard", and the description's test inventory lists no such test.

+export async function readFileText(host: ReviewHost, args: { path: string; ref?: "head" | "base" }): Promise<string> {
+  const { path, ref } = args
+  const pr = await host.pullRequest()
+  const sha = ref === "base" ? pr.base.sha : pr.head.sha
+  const content =
+    (ref !== "base" ? snapshotContent(host.loadedSnapshot(), sha, path) : undefined) ??
+    (await fetchContent(host, pr, path, sha))
+  if (content === undefined) return `${path} does not exist at ${ref ?? "head"} (${sha.slice(0, 7)}).`
+  const out = content
+    .split("\n")
+    .map((line, i) => `${String(i + 1).padStart(5)} | ${line}`)
+    .join("\n")
+  return out.length > MAX_FILE_CHARS
+    ? `${out.slice(0, MAX_FILE_CHARS)}\n... (truncated at ${MAX_FILE_CHARS} characters)`
+    : out

finding.quote: if (this.#failure !== undefined) return { kind: "unavailable", reason: this.#failure }
finding.title: An unavailable search still consumes one of the 40 calls
finding.body: A failed load is remembered for the rest of the run (`this.#failure`), but `access` still charges the call budget before checking it. A model that retries a search after the failure message — a normal agent behaviour — burns the shared 40-call budget for the review and any questions without ever reaching `grep` or `tree`. Don't count a call when the failure is already known, or answer the unavailable message without registering it.
finding.basis: In `access`, the call is counted on every invocation (line 103), and this line then returns `unavailable` for the stored failure, so a model told "Repository search is unavailable" on call 1 keeps spending calls 2–40 on answers that can never succeed.
